thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: sudden spike in 5xx errors for service=model-runner-eu-prod (gateway error + timeouts). error-rate 5m: 18% -> paging threshold breached. metrics: <https://metrics.redwood.example/graph?panel=svc:model-runner>
marc_oncall: I'm up. assigning triage. @anya can you grab runtime logs and check OOM/segfault traces? luis, can you look at infra (node/instance evictions)?
anya_runtime: on it. I see repeated `SIGSEGV` in runner_worker process on a subset of hosts: runner-az1-{07,09,12}. stack trace snippet:
```
#0  0x7f8a2b3c in llm::attention::Kernel::execute(...) +0x1f4
#1  0x7f8a1f9d in runner::ModelExecutor::step +0x2b8
#2  0x55aa3c in main_loop +0x150
```
Also intermittant `OutOfMemoryError` in encoder stage with `malloc` failures in logs. attaching `journalctl -u runner.service` tail: `OOM killer invoked` on node runner-az1-09.
luis_sre: checking node metrics. node-runner-az1-09 has high RSS and kernel logs show swap pressure -> `kswapd` thrash. GPU memory looks fine; CPU + host mem spiking. No autoscaler activity for these hosts in last 12m.
carol_cs: any customer impact? CS dashboard shows 3 customers experiencing elevated latencies and ~15% error rate for inference calls since ~12:08 UTC. I've notified account teams for the impacted orgs.
marc_oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) enable fallback routing to model-runner-small-quant for new requests 2) scale up extra worker nodes in eu-prod group 3) temporarily reduce max_concurrency per-worker to 1 on affected hosts. Can someone run the routing change? devkit-bot can you flip the route? :pray:
devkit-bot: /run route adjust --service model-runner-eu-prod --from=primary --to=fallback --pct=40 --reason="live mitigation"
devkit-bot: done. Traffic shift 40% -> model-runner-small-quant. API: <https://deploys.redwood.example/route/ops/XYZ>
anya_runtime: applied `max_concurrency=1` to runner-az1-{07,09,12} and restarted runner.service on those hosts. also enabled `kvcache` prefix caching for long-running chat sessions to reduce encoder load.
luis_sre: triggered scale: +4 nodes in eu-prod pool (on-demand). Autoscaler will re-evaluate. Also drained runner-az1-12 and moved pods off for deeper inspection.
anya_runtime: collecting coredumps now (gcore + copied logs). command used:
```
for p in $(pgrep runner_worker); do gcore -o /tmp/core.$p $p || true; done
scp root@runner-az1-09:/tmp/core.* infra-logs:/shared/cores/
```
marc_oncall: good. monitor metrics — any reduction in 5xx after route shift and restarts?
anya_runtime: yes: within 3 minutes error-rate down to 8%. request latency for fallback model is slightly higher for long prompts but overall success increased. still seeing occasional segfault on a different host (runner-az1-15) so keep watch.
luis_sre: discovered old kernel module `nv-host-legacy` loaded on runner-az1-09; unloading and reboot plan scheduled for next maintenance window but we did a reboot of runner-az1-12 just now. no immediate sign it's the root cause but environment differs from others.
carol_cs: updated customers: sent initial incident note + ETA for fix. will update once we confirm stable error-rate. :mailbox_with_mail:
marc_oncall: North star next steps: 1) keep traffic shift active 2) continue draining/scrubbing affected nodes 3) collect full backtraces from cores and run `addr2line` mapping 4) prepare rollback to prior model binary if traces point to recent kernel/quant changes. Assign postmortem owners.
anya_runtime: grabbing cores and will run `gdb` backtrace + symbolization. assigning to `anya_runtime` and `luis_sre` for triage. timeline notes: incident started 3654321000, mitigation (traffic shift) at 3654321065, partial recovery at 3654321128.
marc_oncall: any quick mitigation to avoid customer-facing retries? suggest enabling per-route fast-fail to fallback at gateway layer to reduce cascading timeouts.
luis_sre: enabled fast-fail at gateway for model-runner-eu-prod -> fallback at 3654321180. monitoring.
anya_runtime: found a reproducible repro locally when running a long-sequence attention test with `--batch 1 --seq 4096` hitting the same codepath. attaching minimal repro instructions in the postmortem draft.
marc_oncall: solid. if error-rate holds <5% for 10m we'll close paging. keep updates every 5m.
carol_cs: will post customer update in 10m. thanks team. :thumbsup:
marc_oncall: badge: paging -> oncall resolved handoff to runbook owners. Postmortem owners: anya_runtime (root cause analysis), luis_sre (infra correlation), carol_cs (customer comms). follow-up meeting scheduled.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: paging closed (metrics stable) — total duration ~18m. See notes: <https://incidents.redwood.example/3654321000>
marc_oncall: closing thread and creating follow-up GH issue for runtime regression. Thanks all."
